components.css: .ds-room-card{width:340px;overflow:hidden;border:3px solid #20301f;border-radius:.9rem;background:#fffaf0;color:#20301f;box-shadow:5px 6px 0 rgba(32,48,31,.9);font-family:'Trebuchet MS',sans-serif;transition:transform 180ms ease-out,box-shadow 180ms ease-out}.ds-room-card:hover{box-shadow:7px 8px 0 rgba(32,48,31,.92);transform:translate(-2px,-2px)}.ds-room-card:focus-visible{outline:3px solid #2f93d6;outline-offset:4px}.ds-room-poster{display:grid;min-height:140px;place-items:center;border-bottom:3px solid #20301f;background:#ff7526}.ds-room-icon{display:grid;width:76px;height:76px;place-items:center;border:3px solid #20301f;border-radius:1rem 1rem 1rem .25rem;background:#fffaf0;box-shadow:3px 3px 0 rgba(32,48,31,.9);transform:rotate(-3deg)}.ds-room-icon svg{width:42px;height:42px}.ds-room-copy{padding:1.25rem 1.35rem 1.35rem}.ds-status{display:inline-block;padding:.33rem .58rem;border:2px solid #20301f;border-radius:999px;background:#b7e63a;font-size:.7rem;font-weight:900}.ds-room-copy h3{margin:1rem 0 .5rem;font-size:1.8rem;line-height:.98;letter-spacing:-.025em}.ds-room-copy p{margin:0;color:#4a5a47;line-height:1.5}

components.html:
MISATO KATSURAGI@misato.example

Bring one strange idea and one practical question.

REPLY

narrative.overview: Clubhouse borrows its visual world from Martha's Bloom zine language: warm paper, dense green-black ink, imperfect-looking stickers, and saturated print plates. It should feel assembled by a community with opinions, not generated from a generic software dashboard kit. The system is expressive but operational: strong hierarchy keeps room state, membership actions, authorship, and destructive actions immediately legible.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, lightly speckled paper rather than a clean digital canvas.
Heavy editorial type with compact labels and plain, readable body copy.
Thick green-black rules, hard offset print shadows, tape, stamps, and flat shapes.
A distinct colorful IconaMoon pictogram for every room and every interface icon.
Asymmetrical editorial grids on wide screens and an intentional single column on phones.

rules.name: The Paper-and-Ink Rule
rules.body: Every surface must still read clearly with only the paper family and green-black ink; accent colors add identity, never basic legibility.

rules.name: The Spot-Color Rule
rules.body: Use flat saturated plates. Do not soften room identities into pastel gradients or distribute every accent equally across a screen.

rules.name: The One Loud Voice Rule
rules.body: Only the primary page or room title uses display scale. Card titles are forceful, but never compete with the page's first reading stop.

rules.name: The Editorial Rhythm Rule
rules.body: Wide layouts must vary scale or span. Repeated equal cards are not the Clubhouse composition.

rules.name: The Hard Shadow Rule
rules.body: Use hard offset shadows only with an outlined paper or spot-color surface. Never substitute soft glassy elevation or blurred ambient glow.

dos: Do use local IconaMoon files for every interface icon, including loading and empty states.
Do give every room a stable, distinct icon and color treatment.
Do combine thick rules, flat print colors, and hard shadows as one coherent material system.
Do keep access, error, empty, pending, and destructive states as carefully styled as the happy path.
Do reduce motion when the visitor requests it.
donts: Don't fall back to soft SaaS cards, glass panels, ambient shadows, or a uniform dashboard grid.
Don't use emoji, text glyphs, external icon families, or circular spinner artwork as icons.
Don't use color alone to communicate room or post state.
Don't let decorative tape, rotation, or print shapes obscure controls or reading order.
Don't expose Stratos boundary identifiers as visible decoration or UI state.
